question: How many attack drones will Russia launch at Ukraine on the night of October 29–30, 2026?

calls.reasoning: Reference class: Ukrainian Air Force overnight drone-launch counts in October 2026, about 12 nights: 205, 136, 160, 130, 142, 136, 128, 580, 149, 332, 180, 269. Median ≈155, mean ≈210, right-skewed by 'massive' strikes of 400-650 drones roughly every 7-14 days. The last four nights (149, 332, 180, 269) run above early October, and the energy campaign tends to escalate into winter, so I shifted the median up to about 174. I give roughly a 12-15% chance that Oct 29-30 is a massive-strike night, which sets p90 near 400. Trump's claimed Oct 11 'energy ceasefire' failed, so a real truce is a small low tail. Market check: no Polymarket, Kalshi or Manifold contract on nightly drone counts. The Manifold candidates the harness listed concern unrelated events, so I use no crowd anchor.
calls.dossier:
- Air Force overnight launch counts, Oct 2026 (Ukrainian Pravda, Liveuamap, ISW, Ukrinform): Oct 3-4 = 205; Oct 4-5 = 136; Oct 5-6 = 160 (another report says 142); Oct 6-7 = 130 drones + 48 cruise missiles + ballistic (Al Jazeera reports 20+ killed); Oct 7-8 = 142 (82 jet-powered); Oct 8-9 = 136; Oct 13-14 = 128 drones + 39 missiles; Oct 14-15 = 580 (the Wed-Thu span totalled more than 850, ABC/Zelensky); Oct 15-16 = 149 (108 jet-powered); Oct 16-17 = 332 (289 downed, ISW); daytime Oct 17 = 157 (a separate daytime figure, not overnight); Oct 17-18 = 180 + 1 Iskander-M (Ukrainian Pravda Oct 18); Oct 18-19 = 269 drones + ballistic and cruise missiles (Glavred / Ukrinform: 243 drones downed).
- Sept 2026, per the question background: 450+ on Sept 13; 400+ in a 12-hour daytime window on Sept 12. The winter energy campaign began in late Sept.
- Oct 11: Trump announced an 'energy ceasefire' (CNBC/NPR, Oct 12). Russia kept striking and Zelensky said he was 'done' with it. On Oct 18-19 Ukraine launched 1,000+ drones at Russia, hitting St Petersburg oil sites (Al Jazeera, Oct 19). US-Kyiv tensions rose, and retaliation dynamics are possible.
- A Glavred expert comment says Russia may struggle to sustain high-intensity multi-directional drone attacks because of production limits.
- Within the class: about 1 night in 12 in October topped 400 (the Oct 14-15 night, 580); 2 of 12 topped 300; about 7 of 12 fell between 128 and 180. No October night was under 120 in the data found. Earlier 2025-26 data included quiet nights of 16-90 drones.
- Resolves off the Air Force morning report of Oct 30 (overnight launched/detected total, missiles excluded). Daytime counts and multi-day totals do not count.
- Event window: evening of Oct 29 -> morning report of Oct 30 (Kyiv time). As of Oct 19, 0% of the window has elapsed.
- Searched for and did not find: any human prediction market on nightly counts; the full daily list for Oct 9-13 (gaps); any scheduled ceasefire talks for late October.

calls.reasoning: Routine overnight launches in Sep–Oct 2026 cluster at 128–210 drones. Massive combined strikes of 450–650 come roughly every 7–14 nights, so any given night has about a 10–15% chance of being one, which makes the right tail heavy. The last few nights (180, 269) were above the early-October level. The energy campaign is escalating into winter, and Russia may retaliate for Ukraine's 1,000+ drone strike on Russia. Both of these push the median slightly above the routine cluster, to about 166. Production limits and the small chance of a truce make up the low tail. I found no human market on nightly counts.
calls.reconciliation: All three runs agree on the core data: routine nights at 130–210, a massive strike every 1–2 weeks, a 580-drone night on Oct 15 and 269 on Oct 18–19. They also agree that no matching market exists; the harness's Manifold candidates are unrelated contracts. One factual dispute: Run 1 counts Oct 16–17 = 332 as an overnight figure, while Run 3 treats 332 as an ISW day-plus-night total. Run 2 shows that ISW does publish combined totals (337 = 157 day + 180 night for Oct 17–18), which makes Run 3's reading plausible. With no web access on this run I could not settle it, so I gave that data point partial weight. That leaves the median slightly below Run 1's 174 and above Runs 2 and 3 (158–162). How likely a massive strike is on this particular night is a judgment call. Given the recent upward drift and the possibility of retaliation, I put it at about 12–13%, which places p90 at about 380. I kept small escape masses on both sides: below 40 for a lull or pause, above 700 for a record barrage, since a single span has already exceeded 850.
